page: Microsoft Azure D32ds_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Ddsv7 family, built on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor clocked at 4.2 GHz, featuring 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading. Memory resources total 128 GB of RAM, sustaining a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4 GB per virtual core. Storage is provisioned via 1,890 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage, and no hardware GPUs are attached.

Hardware vector and matrix extensions are a distinguishing feature of the Xeon 6973P-C core architecture, which includes AVX-512, AVX-VNNI, and Intel AMX (Advanced Matrix Extensions) for tile and INT8 execution. The CPU cache architecture is particularly large, offering 480 MB of L3 cache alongside 2 MB of L2 cache per core. In benchmarks, the D32ds_v7 exhibits top-tier single-threaded performance, with Geekbench single-core reaching 2,232.0 and single-threaded gzip compression achieving 36.5 GB/sec. Multithreaded benchmarks also place in the upper quartile, including a PassMark CPU score of 54,563.93 and strong throughput in bzip3 decompression and static web serving (59.6 GB/sec).

With 1.89 TB of fast local NVMe SSD space alongside robust general compute and AMX matrix capabilities, the D32ds_v7 delivers balanced hardware density without requiring specialized accelerator tiers. Tradeoffs include standard-tier performance in database operations, raw Redis SET operations, and memory bandwidth, which operate within the middle 50% benchmark segment. The instance is well-suited for high-throughput web serving, CI/CD compilation workloads, enterprise applications requiring local scratch caching, and quantized CPU-based LLM inference.
